clue.text: J Duns' non-U language

indicators.note: non-U says the letter U is to be dropped, punning on the old upper-class/non-upper-class label

parts.note: John Duns Scotus was the medieval Scottish philosopher, so his surname supplies these letters

explanation.surface: A remark that the philosopher Duns Scotus spoke a language not quite upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' was a 1950s label for speech that was not upper class; here it simply means remove U from SCOTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots is the Germanic tongue of lowland Scotland, a language or dialect in its own right.

clue.text: Churchman sadly abused over swindle

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second
sadly suggests the word abused is in a bad way, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A clergyman cruelly mistreated after being cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ABUSED into SUBDEA, and 'over' places it above CON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a minor cleric ranking below a deacon, so a churchman of lower order.

clue.text: Arrangement of biology group

definitions.meaning: a neat sequence or disposition of things
a taxonomic rank grouping related families

explanation.definitionFit: Order means tidy sequence or arrangement, and in biological classification it is the rank between class and family.

clue.text: Make off with your antique in so furtive a manner

parts.note: to steal is to make off with something
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off with your old heirloom in a shifty way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'antique' signals an old-fashioned word: THY for your. 'in so ... a manner' just wraps the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy and furtive both describe moving secretly so as to avoid notice.

clue.text: Perch by the cellar to see this event

indicators.note: by sets one piece beside the next

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod or pole
a vault is an underground cellar

explanation.surface: Sitting on a perch beside the wine cellar to watch some spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read 'vent' for the printed 'event'. A perch, rod or pole is an old British unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole vault is a field event in athletics, jumping a high bar with a flexible rod.

clue.text: Does rain fall so heavily? Hide

definitions.meaning: rain that comes down hard is said to do this
an animal skin with its fur

explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to come down hard like heavy rain, and a pelt is an animal's skin or hide.

clue.text: Action in court as a development of the real thing

definitions.text: Action in court as a development of the real thing

parts.words: Action in court as a development of the real thing
parts.note: not a lawsuit but play on a grassed court, the outdoor game that grew from the older indoor game called real tennis

explanation.surface: A lawsuit seen as an offshoot of a genuine one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action in court' suggests litigation; the court is a sports court. Real tennis is the ancient indoor game from which the modern outdoor game developed.
explanation.definitionFit: The outdoor racket game was devised in the 1870s as an adaptation of real tennis.

clue.text: Old Rover against one Rex

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: An old dog called Rover set against another called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover and Rex look like dog names; a rover here is a sea raider.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse seafaring raiders of the early Middle Ages roved the seas plundering, hence old rovers.

clue.text: Suffered article, in French, on a Cumbrian river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
the Derwent flows through Cumbria in north-west England

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece endured about a river in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is the Lake District county; its River Derwent supplies the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undergone something is to have experienced or endured it, as with suffering.

clue.text: Some ornate style that makes us irritable

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that flowery writing gets on our nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy describes someone short-tempered, easily annoyed or tetchy.

clue.text: Sleeping partner, as Caliban to Trinculo?

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's Tempest the jester sheltering under the monster's gaberdine finds him a strange companion in misery

explanation.definitionFit: A person sharing a bed is literally a sleeping partner; in The Tempest Trinculo crawls under Caliban's cloak, saying misery acquaints a man with strange ones.

clue.text: Renown first of dealers in Arab market rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the built word is read backwards
in places one piece within the market word

parts.note: a souk is a market in an Arab country

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A reputation earned by the leading trader in a Middle Eastern bazaar that was spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives D, which goes inside SOUK to make SODUK; 'rejected' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is Greek-derived praise or prestige, the glory attached to an achievement.

clue.text: One about to return in the city like a ghost

indicators.note: in puts the returning piece inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: to return means the two short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone about to go back into town looking spectral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns IRE into ERI, which 'in' places inside ELY, a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily means in an uncanny, spooky way, the manner of a spectre.

clue.text: Fish, the artist, in mean surroundings

indicators.note: mean surroundings means the word for mean encloses another piece

parts.note: stingy means mean, tight-fisted
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A fish and a painter living in shabby surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as describing the surroundings, but it is the word wrapped round the artist; 'surroundings' is the container signal. RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Faces confronting Snow White in the old thieves' quarter

indicators.note: confronting means facing, the two pieces set against each other

parts.note: Snow White is famous for her companions, the seven dwarfs, so she stands for the number
clock faces are dials

explanation.surface: Clock faces opposite the fairy-tale princess in a criminal district.
explanation.walkthrough: Snow White suggests a colour; it stands for the number of her dwarfs. Seven Dials is a London junction once notorious as a rookery of thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: This road junction near Covent Garden, London, was in the nineteenth century a notorious slum full of criminals.

clue.text: A beggar's cap so superficially attractive?

definitions.text: A beggar's cap so superficially attractive?

parts.words: A beggar's cap so superficially attractive?
parts.note: a cap held out by a beggar is meant to collect small coins, and the word for that describes cheap showy goods

explanation.surface: A tramp's hat made to look appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The beggar's cap literally gathers coins; the adjective describes goods made to sell by surface appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny means cheap and showy, designed to attract buyers rather than to last.

clue.text: Four-letter word creates great disturbance in a vehicle

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters within the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: disturbance means the word great is stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude word causes an uproar on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' is the anagram signal for 'great', and 'in' sets the result inside the vehicle, just after its first letter; 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, from Greek for four and letter.

clue.text: Bugle notes

definitions.meaning: a small tubular glass ... used to trim garments
four letters that are each names of notes on the musical scale

explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a tube-shaped glass ornament sewn on clothes, and B, E, A, D are each musical notes.

clue.text: Evening (or mid-day) service for consumers

parts.note: not a church service but crockery for the main meal, eaten at night or at noon

explanation.surface: A church service in the evening or at noon for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests worship; it is a set of plates. The main meal can be eaten at midday or evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set of matching plates and dishes for the main meal of the day.

clue.text: Annoying chap, putting bulkhead on the harbour vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: the head of the word bulk is its first letter
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships in harbour

explanation.surface: An irritating man fitting a partition on a harbour barge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulkhead' is a ship's partition in the surface, but here it means the head of 'bulk', B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is British slang for a contemptible or irritating fellow.

clue.text: Gilbert's men are said to be crazy

indicators.note: are said to be means the clue word is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: the music-hall song 'Gilbert the Filbert' calls him colonel of the knuts, Edwardian slang for dandies

explanation.surface: W. S. Gilbert's characters are reputed to be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert looks like the librettist; he is 'Gilbert the Filbert, the Knut with a K', a 1914 music-hall song about a dandy. KNUTS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Part of newspaper shows 1 ac tenure, that classical style

parts.note: 1 ac means 1 across, the Scots word; a feu is a Scots form of land tenure
ille is Latin, a classical language, for that
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A newspaper section describing a land holding in a classical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to the answer at 1 across, so 'Scots tenure': a feu is a perpetual lease in Scots law. 'Classical' asks for Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A feuilleton is the section of a European newspaper devoted to literature, criticism or light fiction.

clue.text: Mark Miss German loses on marriage

definitions.meaning: a diacritic sign over a letter
the title for a single German woman bears two dots that the married title lacks

explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot accent; a German Miss is a Fräulein, which carries one, while a wife is a Frau, which does not.

clue.text: My old Pa's revision of sacred choral works

indicators.note: revision of means the preceding words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the possessive is read here as the letters PAS

explanation.surface: Grandad's reworking of some church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges MY OLD PAS. The apostrophe is ignored, so the S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalmody is the singing of psalms, or psalms collectively set to music for worship.

clue.text: 1 ac cloth for a Welsh party?

definitions.meaning: 1 ac means the answer at 1 across, Scots, so a Scottish fabric
the short name of the nationalist party of Wales

explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan woollen fabric of Scotland, and Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party.

clue.text: Topping brown coal to start burning

indicators.note: topping means cutting off the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: First-class brown coal for lighting a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it means remove the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to set alight or catch fire.

clue.text: A solid if pointless misrepresentation of false images

indicators.note: misrepresentation of means the letters before it are presented in a distorted order
pointless means a compass point letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: A firm though futile distortion of untrue pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops S (south, a compass point) from SOLID, leaving OLID; with A, 'misrepresentation of' rearranges AOLID. 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idola, plural of idolum, are Francis Bacon's phantoms or fallacies of the mind, mental illusions.

clue.text: Like Napoleon ere sight of the island which rises here

indicators.note: rises means the word goes upwards in this down entry, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: Napoleon's condition before he caught sight of his island of exile.
explanation.walkthrough: The palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba' is attributed to Napoleon. 'rises' turns ELBA upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The palindrome has the emperor say he was capable or powerful before seeing his exile island.

clue.text: Concern of painters about love, a thing from the heart

indicators.note: about means the painters' concern wraps round the next piece

parts.note: art is what painters work at
love is zero in tennis, and zero is O

explanation.surface: Artists care about romance, something heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside ART to give AORT, then A follows. In tennis scoring love is nil, O.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart's left ventricle.

clue.text: Burden for the old seaman — not for a sportsman, of course

definitions.meaning: in Coleridge's poem the mariner bears the bird he shot hung around his neck

definitions.text: not for a sportsman, of course
definitions.meaning: a golfer on the course scoring three under par finds it no burden

explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner had to wear the dead seabird round his neck, and in golf the term means three under par, no burden on the course.

clue.text: Diet a mess — ruined by a little drink

indicators.note: ruined means the words before it are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A diet spoiled by a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges DIET A MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee, served after dinner.

clue.text: Joint ruled by the big boss

definitions.meaning: a cut of meat for the oven
the thing the dominant person rules, in the old idiom

explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a cut of meat cooked in the oven; the boss is said to rule the roast, an older form of the idiom rule the roost.
